usage: User-supplied validation data only; do not use as production reductions, fit constraints, or AMF boundary conditions.

provenance.change: Only additive interpretation, basis maps, and exact target combinations; original definitions, constants, coefficients, uncertainties and tags are unchanged.
provenance.verification_scope: Exact algebraic representation checks only. No AMF predictions or numerical oracle comparisons are claimed.

rustflow_interpretation.status: Validation fixture for a new finite-density feature; not an input schema already accepted by RustFlow's ordinary or final-state cut APIs.
rustflow_interpretation.component: Full finite-chemical-potential Euclidean integral, including its zero-cut vacuum contribution. Do not substitute a density correction or a single cut term without an independent proof of equality.
rustflow_interpretation.source_powers: The retained powers field has the original sign-dependent dotted convention: positive entries use positive_index_routings, negative entries use negative_index_dot_pairs. Never pass this field unchanged to RustFlow Integral.
rustflow_interpretation.new_powers: finite_density_target.indexed_terms[*].powers uses a single uniform inverse-propagator basis: J(a)=integral product_j rho_j^(-a_j), with the original shifted Euclidean contours and measure. Negative a_j means a numerator power of that same rho_j. These are algebraic target expansions, not IBP reductions or master decompositions.
rustflow_interpretation.input_numerator: finite_density_target.numerator_polynomial uses g<i>_<j>=P_i.P_j for the chemically shifted Euclidean momenta in conventions.momenta. These are not scalar products of the unshifted real loop variables. If an API uses unshifted numerators, explicitly substitute P_i=k_i+i*signature_i*mu*u, u.u=1, including all offsets and medium contractions.
rustflow_interpretation.chemical_assignments: Keep every loop signature and every routed chemical shift sum_i routing[j][i]*signature_i*mu, including loops or denominator slots with zero or negative powers. No graph incidence or cut orientation certificate is supplied by this algebraic dataset; construct and verify those if required by the cutting algorithm.
rustflow_interpretation.physical_mapping: All stored maps are at zero auxiliary mass and zero physical masses, as specified by the oracle. After forming indexed targets, hold their indices and input coefficients fixed under the chosen AMF deformation. A negative power of a shifted slot evolves with that slot. Reconstruct the input combination at the physical endpoint. Derived IBP coefficients can still depend on the auxiliary parameter. A different massive family needs its own mass-dependent physical basis map.
rustflow_interpretation.coordinates: rho and g names are exact polynomial coordinates, not additional integration variables. Polynomial expressions and rational weights use native Symbolica syntax. Array slots are zero-based; momentum labels in names and dot pairs are one-based. The legacy eta_i in conventions.momenta is a chemical signature, not the auxiliary mass parameter; use a distinct symbol for the latter.
rustflow_interpretation.normalization: Retain the original Euclidean measure_factor and normalization exactly. RustFlow's ordinary measure d^D l/(i*pi^(D/2)), Minkowski denominators, and final-state phase-space measures are different conventions. Implement and test an explicit whole-amplitude continuation and normalization adapter, including numerator Wick rotation and cut factors. No global Minkowski sign or phase has been inserted into these coefficients or indexed_terms.
rustflow_interpretation.coefficient_comparison: First compute and save predictions from integral definitions alone. Then form the full Euclidean integral with the stated MSbar measure factor, divide by the unexpanded reference normalization, and compare only supplied Laurent orders. Never expand the normalization a second time or treat a finite zero as an all-orders identity.
rustflow_interpretation.uncertainty_comparison: Supplied absolute uncertainties limit reference agreement; they do not relax the evaluator's separate numerical-stability target. Keep det tags uninterpreted. Exact rational spelling of an uncertain decimal central value does not certify the central value as exact.
rustflow_interpretation.oracle_isolation: Only the validation harness may load constants, coefficients and uncertainties. No production reduction, boundary construction, interpolation, or fit constraints may consume them. Input extraction should pass only bases, conventions needed to define integrals, signatures, and target expressions to evaluation.
rustflow_interpretation.self_contained: All integral definitions and reference values are present in this file. No original attachment, PDF, source checkout, or additional CAS is needed to interpret it.

conventions.expression_syntax: Native Symbolica expressions: explicit multiplication *, powers ^, and functions log(2), zeta(3), exp(x). Parse expression strings with symbolica.E or Expression.parse in native mode. pi and symbolica::γ are built-in constants, not free parameters.

parameters.eps: Dimensional regulator; D=4-2*eps and spatial dimension d=3-2*eps.
parameters.Lambda_bar: Positive MSbar renormalization scale in units where mu=1.

conventions.momenta: For loop i, P_i=(p_i0 + imaginary_unit*eta_i*mu, spatial_p_i), with eta_i=loop_signatures[i-1], real p_i0 integrated from minus infinity to plus infinity, and spatial_p_i in dimension d. imaginary_unit^2=-1. All chemical shifts, including those on loops with zero powers, apply before forming routed momenta and dot products.
conventions.dot_product: Euclidean bilinear product P_a.P_b=(p_a0+imaginary_unit*eta_a*mu)*(p_b0+imaginary_unit*eta_b*mu)+spatial_p_a.spatial_p_b; no complex conjugation.
conventions.measure: For each loop integrate dp_i0/(2*pi) times d^d spatial_p_i/(2*pi)^d, multiplied by measure_factor. Dimensional regularization regulates both UV and IR divergences.
conventions.integrand: Multiply the slot factors over j. For powers[j]=n>0, the factor is 1/(Q_j.Q_j)^n, where Q_j=sum_i positive_index_routings[j][i-1]*P_i. For n=0 it is 1. For n<0 it is (P_a.P_b)^(-n), where [a,b]=negative_index_dot_pairs[j]. Loop labels a,b are one-based; array slots j are zero-based. The integral is this product integrated with the measure for every loop. All propagators are massless.
conventions.coefficients: For L=bases[basis].loops, integral/normalization has the listed Laurent coefficients: sum_k coefficients[k]*eps^k. All original numerical prefactors are already included. Keep normalization unexpanded when comparing. The expansion is supplied through the greatest listed k; all lower unlisted powers are zero, while all higher powers are unspecified. A finite zero does not imply an all-orders zero.
conventions.constants: Substitute the expressions in constants, resolving a8 and a9 through a1. a2, a6, and a10 are the supplied epsilon coefficients, not the complete supplementary series. No unknown a4 coefficient is included.
conventions.uncertainties: uncertainties[k].absolute is the absolute uncertainty of coefficients[k] in the same normalization, obtained from the supplied parenthesized last digits and scaled with the prefactor magnitude. For numerical terms with a supplied uncertainty, rational encoding preserves the decimal central value without making the approximate result exact. The optional det tag is retained as an uninterpreted supplied label; no confidence level or correlation model is specified.
